$comment: The source of sf-input-rich's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js), written in the standard 1.4 form of five authored files; standard simai.smart-component 1.3.11, vocabulary 1.1.5. Larena's request for an editor of its html@1 property type; owner approval q-6df38bf0d7.

size.summary: The field ladder, as sf-textarea's: the frame, the padding and the text of the same size; the toolbar's buttons a rung below.

appearance.summary: How the field looks: a bordered box or a filled one, sf-textarea's two boxes.

label.summary: The visible name of the field; it names the editing surface. Without it the host's aria-label does.

required.summary: The form is not sent while the value is empty (value-missing).

placeholder.summary: Shown while the field holds no text; said as aria-placeholder.

hint.summary: The line under the field; it describes the editing surface.

name.summary: The form name the value is sent under.

rows.summary: The fewest lines the text area shows; it grows with the text.

max-rows.summary: The most lines before the text scrolls inside. Unset means no cap; a value below rows is rows.

disabled.summary: Not editable, not focusable and not sent with the form; a disabled fieldset does the same.

readonly.summary: Read and selected but not changed; the toolbar is disabled, the value is sent.

invalid.summary: The page's verdict: the error look and aria-invalid, with error-message under the field.

error-message.summary: Shown in place of the hint while invalid.

value.summary: HTML of the subset p, h2, h3, h4, strong, em, a[href], ul, ol, li, blockquote, br; href only https:, mailto:, tel: or a /path on the site. Cleaned when it is given and as it is edited; "" when there is no text.

input.summary: The text changed while it is edited: typing, a paste or a drop, a toolbar command, undo or redo; once per change, after the value is cleaned. The native event bubbles from the editing surface, which is its target.

change.summary: The value was committed: the person left the field with a value other than the one it had; a native Event from the editing surface, as a textarea's on leaving it.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.$comment: The editing surface is role textbox, aria-multiline true, named by the label (aria-labelledby) or the host's aria-label, with aria-required, aria-readonly, aria-disabled, aria-invalid, aria-placeholder and aria-describedby the hint or error. The toolbar before it is role toolbar, named by the language file's toolbar word and controlling the surface: one Tab stop, the arrows, Home and End move between its buttons (roving tabindex), each button says aria-pressed where it toggles and aria-keyshortcuts where it has one. Tab in the text leaves the field; it never inserts a tab.

x-summary: A form field for formatted text: paragraphs, headings 2 to 4, bold, italic, links, bulleted and numbered lists and quotes, with a toolbar, undo and redo. Its value is HTML of that subset and nothing else: the value it is given, every paste and drop and every edit are cleaned to it.

x-source.brief: Larena's request for an editor of the html@1 property type (sanitized HTML subset); owner approval q-6df38bf0d7

x-decisions: name: sf-rich-text (owner approval q-6df38bf0d7). A leaf of the field family: the value is a string, the host is the form control through ElementInternals as sf-textarea's, so a form submits the HTML under name and reset puts the value attribute back.

subset: js/rich-text-html.mjs is the one rule, used for the value given, a paste or drop and the surface after every edit. Two readers feed one cleaner -- the browser's parser in an inert <template> where there is a document, a small tolerant string reader where there is none (tests, a server) -- and the output is written from the cleaned model with every text escaped, so it holds nothing off the subset whatever a reader understood.

unwrap, never lose text: an element off the subset is replaced by its text; script, style and the other containers of code, a document's head, drawings and form controls' data (DROPPED) go with their content. An element off the subset that stands as a block (div, section, h1, a table cell, pre) still separates its text from its neighbours', so pasted documents keep their paragraphs.

marks from styles: b and i are strong and em; a word processor's span with a bold or italic style is too, and a b with font-weight normal is not (the wrapper a document editor puts around a whole paste). Only the style's weight and style are read; no attribute survives.

links: https:, mailto:, tel: and a /path on the site; http: is not in the list Larena asked for. The scheme is judged with control characters and white space removed. A link whose href fails becomes its text, on load, paste and in the link editor, which refuses it with the language file's link-invalid word.

normalised value: text outside a block is a p, a block inside a paragraph splits it, a block inside a list item becomes a line of it, a list holds only items, adjacent lists of one kind are one list; no empty block, no line break at a block's edge, nesting a > strong > em; an editor without text is "". The editing surface keeps an empty paragraph's
so the caret has a line, and is cleaned with the same rule in its own mode.

commands: blocks, lists and quotes are the component's own DOM operations; bold and italic use document.execCommand where the browser has it, with a DOM fallback, and the result is cleaned like any edit. Undo and redo are the component's own history of cleaned states with the caret, typing grouped by the second, so neither depends on the browser's undo stack, which a cleaned surface would break.

events: input and change are the native names (§8, §17.3), as sf-textarea's. input once per change after cleaning -- the browser's own input during a command is held back and the command says it once; change when focus leaves the field with a changed value, since a contenteditable has none of its own. Moving between the toolbar, the link editor and the text is not leaving.

toolbar: the class markup of icon buttons (as sf-dropdown and the inherited-value reset draw theirs), so the roving tabindex, aria-pressed and aria-disabled are the field's own attributes in one render; an sf-icon-button host copies its attributes onto its button on its own schedule. Block level is four toggle buttons (paragraph, heading 2, 3, 4) rather than a select: one keyboard model for the whole toolbar, and a select inside a toolbar would be a second form-associated field. Unavailable tools (undo with nothing to undo, a heading inside a list) are aria-disabled and stay reachable.

link editor: sf-popover anchored to the link button, the form's width step (C32), on a phone a sheet at the bottom of the screen lifted into the top layer, holding an sf-input (text, no name, so it is never sent and never blocks the form) and sf-button Apply and Remove link; Enter applies, Escape closes. Its input and change stop at the panel: they are not the field's.

geometry: the frame is sf-textarea's -- the hairline, --sf-radius--ui, the padding calc of each size and the focus ring on the frame -- and the toolbar's buttons are one rung below the field (1/3, 1/2, 1 for sizes 1/2, 1, 2), a block level's text in the glyph's square; headings in the text are the field's text ladder (h2 a rung above the field's text, h3 the field's, h4 a rung below). rows sets the least height in the size's lines, max-rows the most before the text scrolls.

a11y: role textbox with aria-multiline on the editing surface, named by the label or the host's aria-label; toolbar role toolbar with aria-controls. Colours are role tokens only: on-surface on surface-0 and surface-container, the icon button's own pressed look for a pressed tool (on-primary-container on primary-container, C12), on-surface-variant for the hint, placeholder and quotes, error for the error line -- the pairs the theme makes AA in light and dark.
css-variables: seven public variables in sf-textarea's pattern (§6), listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json.

version 1.0.1: the bare editor keeps a page's unlayered :focus-visible outline off with outline: none !important -- an unlayered rule beats every layered one, and drew a second frame inside the frame's ring (owner, 2026-11-01). The frame's ring is unchanged.

version 1.0.3: the editor is unchanged. The subset module it carries (core/js/composition/html-subset.mjs) gains the paste profile of a structured-content editor, cleanTree(tree, {profile: 'paste'}), which keeps pre and simple tables as blocks of their own (simai/ui-source#66); html@1 and every value this editor writes stay as they were.

version 1.1.0: the tag is sf-input-rich (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]); the folder, the id smart.input-rich and the bundle cl-input-rich follow it. sf-rich-text stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the rule, in sheets as :is(sf-input-rich, sf-rich-text) (change journal tag-sf-rich-text-to-sf-input-rich, path-smart-rich-text-to-input-rich).

version 1.1.1 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.1.2 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint snapshots follow the actions block (docs review R031, R032; decisions C13-C15): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws ask for the screen-reader-only utility sheet (sf-button 1.9.0, sf-button-icon 1.7.0), an sf-button-close it draws asks for its own sheet (C14), and sf-input's classes follow its outer sizes (sf-input 1.6.0). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.
version 1.2.0 (2026-11-09): the field is transparent at rest, so it stands on any place (C16, the background system, owner 2026-11-08).

version 1.3.0 (2026-11-10, docs precheck RT-01, RT-02, RT-04, RT-06): a minor, the toolbar, the headings and the link editor drawn by the systems. The block levels P, H2, H3 and H4 stand in the glyph's square, the button rung's line, so they are the icon buttons' square beside them (32 x 32 at size 1 on a desktop, 28 x 28 on a phone; they were 21-32 x 26). The toolbar's buttons are ghost on-surface, the editor toolbar's look of decision C15 (sf-icon-button--ghost; they wrote link, ghost's old name), and a pressed tool wears the icon button's own pressed look (C12: primary container); the field drew secondary container under the icon button's on-primary-container ink. Headings in the text are the field's own text ladder, not the page's: h2 a rung above the field's text, h3 the field's text, h4 a rung below, bold, each with its rung's line (size 1: 20/28, 16/24, 14/20 on a desktop; they were the page's 32/36 and down). The link editor is a form in a popup: the form's width step (--sf-popup-form-width, C32), and on a phone (below 44rem) a sheet at the bottom of the screen, the screen's width up to 44rem, over the scrim, lifted into the top layer (C32 addendum, as sf-menu-context draws a form); at 390 it hung 150 px off the screen. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. The text's padding is unchanged (RT-05): the block padding is the size's tightness step less the hairline, as sf-textarea's and sf-input's, so the text stands one step from the frame's edge. The C16 leftovers' note for 1.2.1 (a pressed toolbar tool wears the icon button's own pressed look; the toolbar's secondary-container rule is gone, C19) ships in this release: 1.2.1 is never released (pair next 2 integration).

html_subset.const: p h2 h3 h4 strong em a[href] ul ol li blockquote br

forbidden_client_responsibilities: trusting the value without the server's own sanitizer

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-input-rich for formatted text a person writes in a form -- a page's text, a description, an announcement -- stored as the HTML subset of Larena's html@1 type.
do_not: Do not trust the submitted value on the server: clean it there with the same subset
Do not use it for one line of text or for code; use sf-input, sf-textarea or sf-code-input
Do not put the value into a page with innerHTML without a sanitizer: render it through the server's cleaned copy or SF.sanitizeHtml
Do not add tags or attributes to the subset in a product; ask for a change of the html@1 type

keyboard: Tab reaches the toolbar (one stop) and then the text; Tab in the text leaves the field
ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End move between the toolbar's buttons
Mod+B and Mod+I toggle bold and italic, Mod+K opens the link editor
Mod+Z undoes, Mod+Shift+Z and Mod+Y redo
Enter in the link editor applies, Escape closes it
accessibility.focus: The frame draws the focus ring while the text has keyboard focus; a click into the text draws none. Toolbar commands keep the caret and the selection in the text; the link editor takes focus when it opens and gives the caret back to the text when it closes.

runCommand.summary: Runs a toolbar command on the current selection: paragraph, heading-2, heading-3, heading-4, bold, italic, link (opens the link editor), bulleted-list, numbered-list, quote, undo, redo. The result is cleaned, recorded for undo and said with input. Returns whether it ran (false while disabled or read-only).

undo.summary: Steps back one cleaned state and says input; false when there is nothing to undo.

redo.summary: Steps forward one cleaned state and says input; false when there is nothing to redo.

rows.section: rename plan R0 (ui-control RENAME-PLAN-2026-11-03), naming decision 2026-11-02
rows.note: the element is sf-input-rich; sf-rich-text is a subclass defined beside it until the date
